descriptions: What a blue Staffy puppy costs with us: £1,500 for a male, £1,700 for a female, a £500 refundable deposit, and UK delivery from £200 to £350 by distance.
Our blue Staffy puppy prices, the refundable deposit, what the price includes and how a puppy gets home — collection from Carlisle or delivery by distance.
Blue Staffy pup sale UK: the two prices, the £500 refundable deposit, the vaccinations, microchip and paperwork included, and what UK delivery costs here.

brief.goal: Rebuild the pup-sale page as the one page on the site that answers the money questions in full — what a puppy costs, what the deposit is and whether it comes back, what the price includes, and what it costs to get a puppy home — so a reader can work out the total before they write to anybody, and can do it without reading the litter page or the why-us page first.
brief.scope: Eleven sections: hero, the three-figure counter strip, the price table, what is included, the delivery table, how the deposit works, the three reviews as a grid, the live puppy grid, a four-row FAQ, the enquiry form and the close. All five migrated images at their original paths and original alt text; the migrated page carried no embed.
brief.done: The page states £1,500, £1,700, a £500 refundable deposit and £200 to £350 delivery and no other money figure; the price and delivery tables stack into labelled rows below 640px; the included list is the six items the migrated body and data/faq.json name and nothing more; all three real reviews and the six live puppies render; four FAQ rows, one of them new and sourced here; one enquiry form that passes the form contract; all five migrated images at their original paths; and no restatement of the £850 to £1,200 band, the four old puppy names, the four percentage counters, the health guarantee, the DM clearance, the twelve-week age or the six delivery cities — and it passes facts-preserved and link parity with nothing missing that `dropped` does not explain.
out_of_scope: the old price band £850 to £1,200 and everything derived from it: data/price-matrix.json holds £1,500 and £1,700 and Known Issue 11 owns the correction; the band is listed in `dropped.prices`
the four named puppies KANE, KOBE, ALIS and BETH: data/puppies.json holds six different dogs and the grid renders those rows; the names are listed in `dropped.names`

the four counters — 100% Vetted, 95% Delivered, 100% 5-star Rated, 24/7 Puppy Support — and '95% On-Time Deliveries': no file on disk holds a vetting rate, a delivery rate, a rating or a support window
a health guarantee of any length or terms: data/settings.json holds guarantee_days null, so no number and no cover may be written
the DM clearance: data/settings.json and the health page's record name L-2-HGA and HC-HSF4 and no third test, so a third clearance here would be a claim the health page contradicts
the twelve-week age of the current litter: data/puppies.json holds no age for any of the six dogs

the six delivery cities — London, Birmingham, Manchester, Leeds, Cornwall and Essex: data/settings.json is Carlisle · Cumbria at town level (Known Issue 16) and project 5 owns the location cluster; no file on disk prices a city
the two invented testimonials — Becky W. of Leeds with the dog Billy, and Daniel H. of Cardiff with the dog Rose: data/reviews.json holds three real reviews and all three are on this page

the case for choosing us — ethical breeding standards, KC lineage, temperament, home raising: /buy-staffy-puppies-for-sale-uk/ is the why-us page (plan Task 16) and this page links it rather than arguing it a second time

the litter listing itself and the three safe buying steps: /buy-blue-staffy-puppies-uk/ is the for-sale listing (plan Task 17) and carries the per-puppy Product and Offer markup; this page marks up the price range as an AggregateOffer so the two pages do not both claim the same offers
the newsletter and waiting-list blocks: no file on disk holds a waiting list, and `tuple.newsletter` is empty on this record

prices: £850 to £1,200 — the migrated page's stated price for a blue Staffy puppy, written three times: in the 'Buy Your Blue Staffy Pup Today – Only £850 to £1,200!' line, as '£850–£1,200 Price Range' in the current-litter section, and in data/facts/blue-staffy-pup-sale-uk.json as the page's whole price set. The band is below the locked prices and predates them (Known Issue 11): data/price-matrix.json holds £1,500 and £1,700 and a £500 refundable deposit, and the `prices` table states those instead.

the four old puppy prices implied by the migrated FAQ's 'Kane, Kobe, Alis, or Beth' reservation line — those four dogs are not in data/puppies.json, which holds Roman, Byrd and Ince at £1,500 and Vennie, Christa and Cheryl at £1,700, and the puppy grid renders the rows that exist. data/page-map.json records the old cards as already removed (refresh_flags old-pup-cards-removed:4), so nothing is deleted here; the names simply are not written back.
'Top-quality Staffies at affordable UK family prices' — an affordability claim measured against nothing. The locked prices are stated plainly and the reader can judge them.
names: Kane, Kobe, Alis and Beth — the four puppies the migrated FAQ names as reservable. They appear in no file on disk; data/puppies.json holds six different dogs and data/page-map.json flags the prose mention (old-pup-names-in-prose:4).

Becky W. of Leeds with the dog Billy, and Daniel H. of Cardiff with the dog Rose — two testimonials and two dogs that appear nowhere in data/reviews.json, which holds three real reviews. All three of the real ones are on this page.

London, Birmingham, Manchester, Leeds, Cornwall and Essex — the migrated page's 'popular delivery locations' list, named twice. data/settings.json is Carlisle · Cumbria at town level (Known Issue 16), no file on disk prices a destination, and project 5 owns the location cluster.
tests: DM — the third clearance in the migrated FAQ's 'clearances for common Staffy conditions (HC, L2HGA, DM)'. data/settings.json names no tests and the health page's record (data/boards/blue-staffy-health-uk.json) carries L-2-HGA and HC-HSF4 and no third; a third test named only here would be a second answer to a question the health page already answers.
creds: 100% Vetted, 95% Delivered, 100% 5-star Rated and 100% 24/7 Puppy Support — the four counters on the migrated hero, plus '95% On-Time Deliveries' in the delivery FAQ. No file on disk holds a vetting rate, a delivery rate, a star rating or a support window, and rule 9 forbids writing a number nobody can check. The kit CounterStrip carries four figures in their place and every one of them is read from data/price-matrix.json or data/settings.json instead.

the health guarantee, named twice ('come with a health guarantee' and, on the migrated review, 'I loved the health guarantee and transparency'). data/settings.json holds guarantee_days null, so there is no term, no length and no cover to state.

'lifetime support from our team of ethical Blue Staffy breeders' — a support commitment with no end date and no file behind it. The page states the email address and the hours from data/settings.json, which is the support that can be evidenced.
text: 'Our 12-week-old blue Staffy puppies are healthy, vaccinated, and ready to join your home.' — the vaccination half is restated in `whats-included`; the twelve-week age is not, because data/puppies.json holds no age for any of the six dogs.

Current Litter: 12-Week-Old Blue Staffy Puppies for Sale UK-Wide — the same age claim as a heading, and it opens the migrated litter paragraph. data/puppies.json holds no age for any of the six dogs, so the age is not written back; the paragraph's own opening sentence IS carried, word for word, as the `puppies` section's lede (verbatim.changed).

'They receive comprehensive health checks, including clearances for common Staffy conditions (HC, L2HGA, DM), and are microchipped before entering their new homes.' — the health check and the microchip are restated in `whats-included`; the three named clearances are not, for the reason in `dropped.tests`, and the page links /blue-staffy-health-uk/ instead.

'All our pups receive comprehensive health checks, are microchipped, and come with a health guarantee.' — the first two clauses are restated in `whats-included`; the guarantee is not, for the reason in `dropped.creds`.
'95% On-Time Deliveries. Trusted DEFRA-approved transport to homes UK-wide.' — the DEFRA-approved transport is restated in `delivery`; the percentage is not, for the reason in `dropped.creds`.
'Don't wait—our current litter won't last long!' — a scarcity line. The buying guide tells a reader to treat sales pressure as a warning sign, and a page that asks for £500 cannot apply it.

'We focus on temperament, raising friendly, confident, and loving companions perfect for families.' and 'Our puppies come from Kennel Club (KC) registered lines, ensuring quality and verifiable heritage.' — two of the four migrated why-us pillars, neither of them an element of the verbatim set (neither H3 contains a target keyword). /buy-staffy-puppies-for-sale-uk/ owns the argument (spec section 2) and `why-choose` states each pillar in one sentence instead. The fourth pillar's opening, 'Our commitment to responsible breeding means healthy parents and happy puppies, always.', IS in the set and is carried verbatim under 'Ethical Breeding Standards'.

'Please ensure your mobile number is correct for prompt communication regarding your puppy inquiry.' — the migrated form's note. ContactFormKit renders its own note, and data/settings.json holds PHONE_PLACEHOLDER: we do not ring, we reply by email (project 6 owns the phone).

100% Vetted 95% Delivered 100% 5★ Rated 100% 24/7 Puppy Support — the migrated hero's four counters, with the VIEW PUPPIES button above them and the why-us heading beneath. No file on disk holds a vetting rate, a delivery rate, a star rating or a support window (working rule 9, dropped.creds). The kit CounterStrip carries four figures in their place and every one of them is read from data/price-matrix.json or data/settings.json.

Buy Your Blue Staffy Pup Today – Only £850 to £1,200! — the migrated litter section's own eyebrow, and the loudest of the three places the old band was written. It predates the locked prices (Known Issue 11): data/price-matrix.json holds £1,500 and £1,700, and the `prices` table states those. dropped.prices carries the band itself.

£850–£1,200 Price Range. — the same band again, as a sentence at the end of the migrated litter paragraph. Excised where that paragraph is carried (verbatim.changed) rather than restated wrongly or duplicated beside the price table.

We pride ourselves on being ethical Blue Staffy breeders UK —100% Health Checked. — the '100% Health Checked' half is one of the migrated hero's four unevidenced counters and working rule 9 forbids writing a number nobody can check (dropped.creds). The clause is excised from the `sale-kc-health-checked` FAQ answer, which carries every other word of the migrated answer, and the excision is recorded in verbatim.changed.
links: #Staffies-leaving and #contact-us — the migrated page's two in-page anchors, both pointing at fragments of the WordPress layout that no longer exists. The rebuilt page's own section ids are the jump targets and are owned by nav-anchors-resolve.

changed.old: Blue Staffy Pup Sale UK: Your Perfect Match Awaits!
changed.new: What A Blue Staffy Puppy Costs With Us
changed.reason: the breeder's approved pick, confirmed 2026-09-21. `approval.h1` is 2, and the ground is this record's own `sections[top].why`: the migrated H1 states no figure, and this outline moves the money to the top of the page precisely because the migrated page opened on a headline with nothing in it and put the only price — a band that is now wrong — six screens down. The replacement says what the page does: it states what a puppy costs here. 'Your Perfect Match Awaits!' also promises a match, which is a claim about a reader rather than about a dog and rests on no file on disk (working rule 9). Nothing the old wording identified is lost: the slug's own phrase is the picked title, and the rebuilt page writes 'Blue Staffy pup sale UK' once, in the hero lede under the H1, where it names what the page is rather than decorating it. This is the one element of the set the breeder changed by choosing between variants rather than the rewrite repairing a fact, and it is recorded here for that reason.
